question.text: In a chemical reaction, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mover><mo>⇌</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mover><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math> , the initial concentration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> was <math><mn>1.5</mn></math> times of the concentration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> , but the equilibrium concentrations of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> were found to be equal. The equilibrium constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mfenced></math> for the chemical reaction is:

solution.text:
A      +      2B      ⇌       2C    +    D
Initial conc. of [A] = a , [B] = 1.5a , [C] = 0 and [D] = 0

At equilibrium [A] = (a - x) , [B] = 1.5(a - 2x) , [C] = 2x and [D] = x

At equilibrium a-x=1.5a-2x

0.5 a=x

a=2x

kC=2x2xa-x1.5a-2x2=4x2.xxx2=4
